frontend.note: Preparation evidence advances the frontend head. The issued token binds the pushed preparation commit, not this observation.

userOutcome.operationalQuestion: Can an authorized actor read, correct, submit and decide one timecard through a deterministic state machine without self-approval, duplicate effects or legacy dual-write?
userOutcome.primaryAction: review a timecard, record an immutable correction, submit it, and perform an independent decision with a durable receipt
userOutcome.pageArchetype: timecard workspace with period ledger, correction history, state-aware actions and command recovery
userOutcome.boundedOutcome: one canonical timecard aggregate and TimecardDecisionRecorded.v1 event replace partial legacy behavior while activation remains off

included: canonical timecard aggregate, application service, repository, controller and owner PEP integration
correction ledger, submit transition, independent decision and originating-scope command receipt
maker-checker constraints against worker, submitter and latest correction maker
idempotency, expected-version CAS and immutable TimecardDecisionRecorded.v1 outbox publication
V11 clean and V10-to-V11 forward ledger migration
least-privilege publisher ACL update in the allocated Time migration configuration
accessible canonical timecard frontend without switching legacy callers
excluded: legacy shared-utils, HCM workspace, route or shell cutover
dual read or dual write between legacy and canonical timecard implementations
clock ingestion, leave, schedule, payroll or provider integrations
feature enablement, customer data, policy activation or production release

moduleAllowedBackend: dwp-time-server/src/main/java/com/dwp/services/time/TimeDatabaseMigrationConfiguration.java (V11 registration and least-privilege publisher ACL only)

runtimeSecurityRollout.tenantContext: trusted Gateway/owner context plus repository isolation; request body and browser-supplied trusted headers are never authoritative
runtimeSecurityRollout.population: SELF or TARGET_POPULATION according to the exact v42 route profile
runtimeSecurityRollout.idempotency: same key and canonical request digest returns the original receipt; mismatched reuse fails with no side effect
runtimeSecurityRollout.optimisticConcurrency: all commands require expected version and stale CAS fails without side effects
runtimeSecurityRollout.featureFlag: module-owned TIM-017 flag if one is needed

implementationOrdering.beforeStartToken: Pin the corrected v42 authorization/OpenAPI/Gateway/AsyncAPI control bridge, reserve V11, and materialize clean dedicated worktrees.
implementationOrdering.afterStartToken: Implement the Time timecard owner slice and TIM frontend only within the sealed touch manifest, then commit and push module branches without switching legacy callers or merging dwp-dev.
implementationOrdering.antiCircularityRule: TIM runtime implementation and its acceptance tests are module deliverables and are not prerequisites for issuing the token that authorizes them.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: All five owner/browser operations conform to the sealed timecard, command and receipt transport contracts with no shadow DTO drift.
The canonical synthetic timecard fixture follows stable ledger totals, corrections, state and receipt hashes.
Wrong tenant, subject, population, field group, purpose, closed period or approval scope is denied before disclosure.
Only the sealed eight-state precedence and allowed transitions are accepted; LOCKED, CLOSED and SUPERSEDED cannot be bypassed.
A worker, submitter or latest correction maker cannot decide the same timecard and direct/delegated authority is re-evaluated at decision time.
Exact replay returns the original receipt; mismatched key reuse and stale CAS create no correction, transition, decision, receipt or event.
A successful decision emits exactly one immutable minimized TimecardDecisionRecorded.v1 fact and never emits the unsuffixed alias.
V11 passes clean and V10-to-V11 upgrade and introduces the canonical ledger by forward migration without editing V10.
The Time publisher receives only the exact V11-owned privileges required for canonical decision publication.
The canonical implementation does not switch or duplicate legacy readers/writers; later cutover remains a separately controlled task.
The UI proves failure, partial data, command recovery, keyboard, focus, accessible naming, high contrast, reduced motion and 200-percent zoom behavior.

verificationPlan.policy: CHANGED_CLUSTER_FIRST_THEN_SLICE_CONTRACT_AND_ONE_MODULE_BATCH; do not rerun broad repository suites after each finding.
backend: timecard transport, eight-state and golden-fixture tests
maker-checker, idempotency, CAS, receipt and atomic outbox tests
V11 clean and V10 upgrade tests plus exact publisher ACL assertion
frontend: one TIM-017 slice test covering failure/recovery/accessibility and no-dual-write
final: clean module branches pushed without merging dwp-dev

deliverables: backend and frontend module branch commits and upstream push evidence
all eleven acceptance results with exact test commands
V11 clean and V10-to-V11 upgrade evidence
authorization, maker-checker, idempotency, CAS, receipt and exactly-once event evidence
changed-path manifest proving control-only and protected paths were not edited
stopConditions: V11 appears or the TIME_MAIN high-water changes before activation.
Any required v42 route, timecard schema, event or checksum drifts from the pinned control bridge.
Implementation requires a control-only, protected, shared-utils, HCM, shell, route or other-module path.
A targeted test disproves a sealed state, maker-checker, idempotency, CAS, receipt, ACL or event invariant.
Dual read/write, feature activation, customer data, external integration or production release is attempted.
